THE_QUESTION: Was V1's failure primarily caused by repeatedly rehearsing a small 428-state bank, and does increasing strategic-state diversity improve held-out latent crossover without changing architecture or compute?

unchanged: z1 rollout Pole B OP7 no overlay
oracle-gated rehearsal rule (exact Delta labels, ties zero pressure)
fresh step-0 model (no V1 checkpoint continuation)

REHEARSAL_BANK.minimum_rule: If legacy+new eligible < 1500 after the frozen 320-seed block completes, V2 training remains BLOCKED; no adaptive seed extension.
REHEARSAL_BANK.NO_MARGIN_FILTER: All resolvable states (Delta != 0) from both sources; no |Delta|>=2 filter.

SUPERSEDED_BY_OG_PSP.note: the bank-only run spec is SUPERSEDED and must not be launched
SUPERSEDED_BY_OG_PSP.why: The crossed FIT/CALIB measurement showed the 'wrong' latent matches each teacher within ~2 percentage points of the 'right' one (94.7 vs 93.0 on FIT A-preferred; 96.2 vs 94.1 on B-preferred) with z0-z1 JSD of 0.0051 bits. V1 did not produce specialised latents that failed to transfer -- it produced a single state-conditional imitator with essentially no latent content. A larger bank improves that map's generalisation but has no mechanism to create latent differentiation, so bank size alone was the wrong lever.
SUPERSEDED_BY_OG_PSP.what_survives: The 320-seed collection itself. It is useful supervision for the corrected treatment and was allowed to finish rather than discarded.
SUPERSEDED_BY_OG_PSP.preserved_not_rewritten: This record is annotated rather than edited so the project's original reasoning, and the fact that it was later corrected, both remain visible.
